items.followUp: How are the formed elements separated from plasma in a blood sample?

rubric.why: Names the method used to separate plasma from blood.
rubric.description: Blood is centrifuged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying centrifugation as the method.

rubric.why: Describes the separation produced by centrifugation.
rubric.description: Blood cells settle while plasma remains as the upper layer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the plasma layer or the separation of cells and plasma.

modelAnswer: A blood sample is placed in a centrifuge and spun.
The heavier blood cells settle at the bottom, leaving plasma as the upper layer.

items.followUp: Name the main structures through which water is lost from a plant during transpiration.

rubric.why: Stomata are the main structures for transpiration.
rubric.description: Stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming stomata.

rubric.why: Transpiration also occurs through the cuticle and lenticels.
rubric.description: Cuticle or lenticels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming either cuticle or lenticels.

modelAnswer: Transpiration mainly occurs through the stomata.
It also occurs through the cuticle and lenticels.

items.followUp: Define transpiration and explain how humidity, wind and temperature affect its rate.

rubric.why: States the meaning of transpiration.
rubric.description: Transpiration is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining transpiration as water-vapour loss from a plant, especially its aerial parts.

rubric.why: Light affects the opening of stomata and thus transpiration.
rubric.description: Light generally increases transpiration by promoting stomatal opening.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying light as a factor affecting the rate.

rubric.why: Temperature influences evaporation and the rate of water loss.
rubric.description: Higher temperature generally increases transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming temperature and its effect.

rubric.why: The moisture level of the air affects water-vapour diffusion from leaves.
rubric.description: High humidity decreases transpiration; low humidity increases it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming humidity and stating its effect.

rubric.why: Air movement removes moist air around leaves and affects water loss.
rubric.description: Wind generally increases transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming wind or air movement as a factor.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the leaves.
Light generally increases transpiration by promoting the opening of stomata.
Higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation and transpiration.
High humidity decreases transpiration, while low humidity increases it.
Wind generally increases transpiration by removing moist air around the leaves.

items.followUp: State two causes of deforestation and two ways it can reduce biodiversity.

rubric.why: Clearing forests for agriculture is a cause of deforestation.
rubric.description: Agricultural expansion or clearing land for cultivation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying agricultural land-clearing.

rubric.why: Human demand for wood, land and development contributes to deforestation.
rubric.description: A further valid cause, such as timber or fuelwood collection, urbanization, population growth or industrial development.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one additional valid cause.

rubric.why: Forest clearing removes habitats needed by species.
rubric.description: Loss or destruction of habitats.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying habitat loss.

rubric.why: Species may disappear when their habitats and resources are destroyed.
rubric.description: Extinction of species or loss of species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying extinction or loss of species.

rubric.why: Deforestation reduces biological variety and can disrupt ecosystem relationships.
rubric.description: Reduced biodiversity or disruption of ecosystems and food chains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a further effect on biodiversity or ecosystem relationships.

modelAnswer: Deforestation is caused by clearing forests for agriculture and cultivation.
Other causes include cutting trees for timber or fuelwood, urbanization, population growth and industrial development.
It destroys habitats and leaves organisms without places to live.
Species may decline or become extinct.
Consequently, biodiversity decreases and ecosystem relationships may be disrupted.

items.followUp: Describe the three main stages of aerobic respiration and state where each occurs.

rubric.why: Identifies glycolysis and its main change or location.
rubric.description: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and breaks glucose into pyruvic acid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the location and/or the conversion of glucose to pyruvic acid.

rubric.why: Identifies the Krebs cycle and a key feature or location.
rubric.description: The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix and releases carbon dioxide while producing energy carriers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the cycle's location or a correct product/role.

rubric.why: Identifies the electron transport chain and its location or role of oxygen.
rubric.description: The electron transport chain is on the inner mitochondrial membrane; oxygen accepts electrons and forms water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the location or the role of oxygen and formation of water.

rubric.why: Shows how the stages contribute to energy release in respiration.
rubric.description: Energy is transferred to ATP, especially during the electron transport chain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating ATP production or the energy carriers involved.

modelAnswer: Cellular respiration is the process in which cells break down glucose and release energy, which is transferred to ATP.
Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and breaks glucose into pyruvic acid, producing a small amount of ATP and NADH.
In the mitochondrial matrix, the Krebs cycle oxidizes products of pyruvic acid breakdown, releasing carbon dioxide and producing energy carriers.
In the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membrane, electrons pass along carriers; oxygen accepts electrons and forms water, and much ATP is produced.

items.followUp: Name the two compound tissues in plants and state what each transports.

accept: more than one type of cell
rubric.why: Defines compound tissue as a tissue made of different cell types working together.
rubric.description: A compound tissue consists of different kinds of cells that perform a common function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for distinguishing compound tissue from a tissue made of one cell type.

rubric.why: Identifies xylem's transport function.
rubric.description: Xylem transports water and mineral salts, mainly from roots to the rest of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming xylem and its transport function.

rubric.why: Names components of xylem.
rubric.description: Xylem includes tracheids, vessels, fibres and parenchyma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two xylem cell types.

rubric.why: Identifies phloem and its function or components.
rubric.description: Phloem transports food and includes sieve tubes and companion cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming phloem with its function or at least two of its cell types.

modelAnswer: Compound tissues are made of different kinds of cells that work together to perform a common function.
Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, fibres and parenchyma; it transports water and mineral salts through the plant.
Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma; it transports food from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

items.followUp: What are bioelements, and in what form are they usually found in living organisms?

rubric.why: States that bioelements do not occur as isolated elements in living organisms.
rubric.description: Bioelements are not found in an isolated or free form in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bioelements are not isolated.

rubric.why: States that bioelements are combined into molecules or compounds.
rubric.description: They occur chemically combined in compounds or biomolecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are chemically combined in molecules, compounds or biomolecules.

modelAnswer: Bioelements do not occur in living organisms in an isolated form.
They are chemically combined with one another in molecules and compounds, including biomolecules.

items.followUp: Name Avicenna's famous medical book and state one field in which he was renowned.

rubric.why: Identifies Bu Ali Sina/Avicenna as a notable scholar or physician.
rubric.description: Bu Ali Sina, also known as Avicenna, was a renowned Muslim physician and scholar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying him as a physician or notable scholar.

rubric.why: Gives the title of his famous medical book.
rubric.description: His famous book is The Canon of Medicine (Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct book title.

modelAnswer: Bu Ali Sina, also known as Avicenna, was a renowned Muslim physician and scholar.
His famous book is The Canon of Medicine, also known as Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb.
